facts.raw_span: a one-week history of epigastric pain
hematemesis
no significant medical or surgical history
took no medications
a smoker
did not drink alcohol
vital signs were stable
the abdomen was soft without tenderness
a rectal examination revealed no melena
a hemoglobin level of 6.3 g/dL

concepts.why: The patient has a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa and a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass measuring 6×5 cm with fat attenuation in the antropyloric region, which is consistent with a gastric lipoma.

The patient presents with epigastric pain and hematemesis, and upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa, which is consistent with a gastric ulcer.
The patient presents with hematemesis and a low hemoglobin level, which is consistent with gastrointestinal bleeding.
The patient has a low hemoglobin level, which is consistent with anemia.

rationales.F01: Epigastric pain is a common symptom of gastric issues, but not specific to any one condition.
rationales.F02: Hematemesis is a strong indicator of gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F10: A low hemoglobin level indicates anemia, which can be caused by gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F11: The presence of a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration is highly suggestive of a gastric lipoma or gastric ulcer.
rationales.F12: The CT scan results showing a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation are highly suggestive of a gastric lipoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa and a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation on CT strongly supports Gastric lipoma.
